solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poem is read to pals wrongly

indicators.note: letters put together wrongly are scrambled into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, twelve letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone recites verse to friends but gets it all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' rearranges the letters of IS READ TO PALS into Milton's epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic about the Fall of Man is one of the best-known long poems in English.

clue.text: Ones having very little bread?

parts.note: reads like people short of a loaf, but bread is slang for money, so these are the very poor

explanation.definitionFit: Destitute people have almost no money, and bread is slang for cash.

clue.text: Potato pulled up around engineers in secluded site

indicators.note: the reversed potato goes around the engineers
in a down clue, pulled up means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: tater is an informal word for a potato
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up a potato near where the engineers are working in a quiet spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' makes RETAT; 'around' wraps it round the engineers. Tater is informal for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet, secluded place where one goes to withdraw from the world.

clue.text: Daughter lacking balance in Bedfordshire town

parts.note: something lacking balance is unsteady or unstable

explanation.surface: A girl is wobbly on her feet in an English county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedfordshire is a county north of London; Dunstable is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunstable is a market town in the south of the English county of Bedfordshire.

clue.text: Wrong road for peninsula

parts.note: a wrong or misdeed is a sin
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone takes a wrong road towards a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 runs from London to Edinburgh; crosswords write its 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinai is the triangular peninsula in Egypt between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba.

clue.text: Rules do change in place of pilgrimage

indicators.note: letters that change their arrangement form a different word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The rules are altered at a holy shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges RULES DO.
explanation.definitionFit: The French town in the Pyrenees draws millions of Catholic pilgrims to its Marian grotto.

clue.text: Moral consideration? It's of little weight

definitions.meaning: a qualm of conscience that stops one acting
an old apothecaries' unit of weight, twenty grains

explanation.definitionFit: A scruple is both a moral hesitation and a tiny apothecaries' weight of twenty grains.

clue.text: Teens stopping for recreation-feature across stream?

indicators.note: read as re-creation, the letters are created afresh in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, thirteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Teenagers stop to play by a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' is the anagram signal, read as re-creation, and rearranges TEENS STOPPING. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping stones are flat stones set in a stream so walkers can cross it.

clue.text: At first glance, how a clock is read?

definitions.meaning: the time is read from the dial of a clock, literally on its face

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means judging by appearance, and literally the time is read from a clock's dial.

clue.text: Dig supported by market town

parts.note: a dig is a jibe or taunt
something supported by another rests on it

explanation.surface: A sly jibe lands in a provincial town.
explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton, in Somerset, is a historic English town known for its markets.

clue.text: One turn diverted part of atom

indicators.note: letters that are diverted are sent off in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A single turn sends a particle off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges ONE TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: This uncharged particle sits in the nucleus of an atom along with protons.

clue.text: Advertising flaw initially exposed powerful figure in school

parts.note: PR is public relations, the business of promotion

indicators.note: exposed means stripped, so the word loses its initial letter

parts.note: a flaw is a defect

explanation.surface: An advertising error reveals a dominant figure at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially exposed' strips the flaw of its opening letter, leaving EFECT; PR is public relations, the advertising trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefect is a senior pupil given authority over others in a British school.

clue.text: Thoroughly popular department in front of hospital

indicators.note: the first pieces come before the next one

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
H is the abbreviation for hospital on signs and maps

explanation.surface: A well-liked hospital department works with great care.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something examined thoroughly and in great detail.

clue.text: Part of magazine hidden in main settee

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of a magazine has been lost down the back of the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across mai-N SET-tee.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is an extra page or small section placed inside a magazine.

clue.text: Support for a lot of titles?

definitions.text: Support for a lot of titles?

parts.words: Support for a lot of titles?
parts.note: suggests patronage of the nobility, but the titles are books standing on a shelf

explanation.definitionFit: A shelf holds up a row of volumes, each a title in the publishing sense.

clue.text: Published journalist trapping fool beaten for ingenuity

indicators.note: the first pieces enclose the next one

parts.note: out means published or released
a twit is a fool
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman exposes a fool who was beaten in a battle of wits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' sets the fool after the first two letters of the outed journalist; 'beaten for ingenuity' is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outwitted is to be outdone by someone cleverer.

clue.text: Bird beginning to go by grey ridge

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: grey suggests old age
a crest is the top ridge of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird sets off along a grey ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldcrest is Europe's smallest bird, with a bright yellow crown stripe.

clue.text: Drunk in squalid hole in African country

indicators.note: the drunk goes inside the other piece
squalid suggests mess, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk sits in a filthy hovel somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squalid' makes LEHO, and 'in' places the drunk at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a mountainous kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Man from church overlooking French city

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece overlooking another sits above it

parts.note: Arles is a city in Provence

explanation.surface: A man from a church gazes down on a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles is a man's name, so any Charles is an example of a man.

clue.text: Reckon wine in audience is for this purpose

indicators.note: what an audience hears is spoken, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: reckon means add up, and hock is a German white wine

explanation.surface: Someone tots up the wine while watching a show for a particular occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in audience' says ADD HOCK is heard; HOCK is a German white wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means arranged for one particular purpose only.

clue.text: Culpable volunteers put up with poor service

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
in tennis a fault is a bad serve

explanation.surface: Volunteers to blame for putting up with bad service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TA into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at fault is to blame, which is what culpable means.

clue.text: A Bible kept in rigorous university

indicators.note: the first pieces are kept inside the next

parts.note: rigorous means hard or demanding
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A Bible is held in a strict university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' places the A and the Revised Version inside the word for rigorous.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvard, in Massachusetts, is the oldest university in the United States.

clue.text: Suspect cuts linked to some Italian region

indicators.note: suspect suggests something not right, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: some and any are interchangeable in many sentences

explanation.surface: Suspicious cuts are linked to part of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' rearranges CUTS into TUSC.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is the region of central Italy around Florence.

clue.text: Some gentle doyen promoted song

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved up, read backwards
some says part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A gentle elder statesman is given a higher post and a tune.
explanation.walkthrough: gentLE DOYen holds LEDOY, which 'promoted' turns upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A yodel is a song sung with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Horrific place? Deduce a negative response

parts.note: to deduce is to infer
no is a negative answer

explanation.surface: Someone works out that the answer to a request is no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: Inferno is Dante's hell.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a hellish blaze, and Dante's Inferno is hell itself, a horrifying place.

clue.text: Edward taking in championship I forgot is annoyed

indicators.note: the first piece takes the next inside it

parts.note: Ned is a pet form of Edward

indicators.note: the I is forgotten, so it drops out

parts.note: a title is a championship win

explanation.surface: Edward, having forgotten the title, is irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgot' leaves TTLE once the I goes; 'taking in' sets that inside the pet name for Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettled means irritated, as if stung by a nettle.

clue.text: Destructive wave woman detected in swirling mist

indicators.note: the woman is found inside the other piece
something swirling is churned around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Una is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman is spotted in a swirling sea mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes TSMI, and 'detected in' places the woman within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave, usually caused by an earthquake, that devastates coasts.

clue.text: Cheered about lawyer in appeal and made stronger?

indicators.note: the first word goes around the others

parts.note: consoled means comforted or cheered

indicators.note: the lawyer goes inside the appeal

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal
DA is a US district attorney

explanation.surface: Someone is cheered when a lawyer appeals and their case is strengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives IDAT, and 'about' wraps the word for cheered around it; IT as sex appeal is an old slang sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To consolidate is to strengthen, so consolidated means made stronger or firmer.
